item.title: Newscast - Friday, March 20, 2026
item.description: In this newscast: The Juneau Police Department is seeking assistance in locating a 17-year-old boy who has been reportedly missing for two days; Juneau's legendary Gold Medal Basketball Tournament kicks off this weekend for the 77th time; Juneau Police commander Matt DuBois speaks with KTOO's Mike Lane about a regional task force that investigates illegal drugs being distributed in Southeast Alaska; The Kodiak Island Borough School District is not recruiting international teachers for next fall

item.title: Juneau School District reaches tentative agreement with teachers union
item.description: The tentative agreement is awaiting ratification from the union and approval from the Juneau School Board.

item.title: Alaska lawmakers look to resolve standoff over fast-track budget bill
item.description: Lawmakers appointed a conference committee after prior versions of the bill failed to garner support from House Republicans to spend from savings.

item.title: Alaska education board takes steps to assess boarding school conditions after outcry
item.description: The state board will create a new committee to review concerns, including student services and maintenance needs after roughly a quarter of students disenrolled this year.

item.title: Juneau high schoolers travel to Hawaii to help rebuild homes destroyed by Lahaina wildfires
item.description: Students enrolled in the Juneau School District’s House Build program are eligible to join the annual Habitat for Humanity build trip in Hawaii.

item.title: Kipnuk votes to relocate following devastation from Halong
item.description: More than 92% of adult tribal members that the tribe was able to contact by phone in recent weeks voted to relocate. Of two potential relocation sites located between Kipnuk and Chefornak, two-thirds said they'd prefer an option closer to the historical settlement of Cicing.

item.title: Dunleavy proposes property tax breaks for Alaska LNG pipeline
item.description: The bill would replace most local property and sales taxes with a tax on the volume of gas flowing through the pipeline. It would likely amount to a significant tax cut for the project.

item.title: Forest Service plans to hold virtual meeting on Tongass Forest Plan revision Wednesday
item.description: The virtual meeting has been added to a calendar of in-person meetings in communities around Southeast.

item.title: Juneau breaks March snowfall record, but not the winter record yet
item.description: This is the snowiest March the city has seen since consistent record keeping began in 1943. But after a data correction, the city is 1.2 inches from beating the overall winter record.

item.title: Newscast - Monday, March 23, 2026
